rationale: The same two Sabbath scenes, in the same order, with the same question, "Have you not read" / "Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry" (Matthew 12:3; Mark 2:25, BSB), the same ruling ("the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath" / "Lord even of the Sabbath," Matthew 12:8; Mark 2:28), and the same command, "Stretch out your hand" (Matthew 12:13; Mark 3:5). Parallel/strong rather than explicit, following conn-matt9-paralytic-mark2, because neither Gospel names the other and the differences are real and checkable in the BSB. Only Mark names "Abiathar" (2:26) and has "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath" (2:27). Only Matthew has the priests in the temple, "something greater than the temple," and the second quotation of Hosea 6:6 (12:5-7), and only Matthew has the sheep in the pit (12:11-12). In Mark, Jesus asks the question, "Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?" (3:4); in Matthew the opponents ask "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" (12:10). Mark alone notes Jesus' "anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart" (3:5) and adds that the Pharisees plotted "with the Herodians" (3:6).
